name: Maxence Lacroix
biography_en:
Maxence Lacroix joined Chelsea in July 2026 when he signed a contract until 2032. The France international defender moved across London from Crystal Palace.
He arrived at Stamford Bridge with the reputation of being among European football’s most commanding centre-backs, as well as one of the fastest and best aerial defenders in the Premier League.

He made 98 appearances for Crystal Palace during two seasons at Selhurst Park and made history with the Eagles by winning the UEFA Conference League, FA Cup and Community Shield.

Prior to playing in England, Lacroix began his career in his homeland and also played in Germany. He is a product of Sochaux's academy and made 28 senior appearances for the French club’s first team before joining Wolfsburg in August 2020.

He spent four years with the German side and made 130 appearances before his switch to south London.

Lacroix’s performances in the Premier League and in Europe with Palace earned him international recognition in March 2026, when he made his debut for France. He was then included in Les Bleus’ squad for the FIFA World Cup later that year and made three appearances at the tournament as his country claimed a fourth-place finish.

Lacroix made his Chelsea debut when he started the first Premier League game of the season, a derby away at Fulham, and he was credited with an assist for Morgan Rogers goal in a 3-2 victory.
